ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider's original payment method; no driver flag (driver never marked arrival, so NS-2's flag_account trigger does not apply).
ruling.reasoning:
The rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance, so the NS-4 route (rider cancelled later than 3 minutes) is the one engaged: cancelled_by = rider, 200 s after acceptance [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. Under NS-4 the $5.00 fee is chargeable only as a genuine late-cancellation charge, and the $5.00 on record is the amount in dispute [F2][F6].

The record shows the driver never actually reached the rider: closest approach 2137 m at 21:28:55, never within 200 m, and driver_arrived_at is null [F1][F4]. No arrival confirmation exists — no "I'm Here" tap and no automatic arrival [F5]. The driver's own chat says "About 5 min, traffic" at 21:27 [F9], i.e. he was still some minutes out when the rider cancelled [F2]. NS-4's charge presupposes the charged case in A1 — the driver pressed "I'm Here", waited, and the rider no-showed; that premise is absent here [F4][F5][NS-4]. The fee therefore cannot stand as a no-show/wait charge and must be refunded in full.

Because this is a rider-cancellation case, no NS-1 condition can be satisfied: no arrival event with GPS within 200 m [F1][F4][F5], and only 1 in-app message with 0 in-app calls before cancellation [F3]. The driver's post-hoc statement ("I was on my way when the rider cancelled") is a statement, not consent or evidence of arrival, and system records override it [F11].

Traffic data does not help: no incidents near the route, and the only speed-band entry (Pasir Panjang Drive, band 6) is a free-flowing segment [F12][F13]. Weather fair, no surge (1.0×) [F14][F7]. Profiles (rider 0 disputes; driver 1 upheld no-show) never decide the case and are not relied on [F15][F16][RD-6 / NS-9 n/a]. The amount refunded is the fee on record: $5.00 [F6]; NS-4/§2.2.

Safety screen: I read both chat messages [F8][F9], the driver's statement [F11] and the complaint [F2]; none contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern = none [SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: who cancelled and when, the fee, and the absence of any arrival record are all settled by timestamped records [F2][F4][F5][F10].

element_findings.reason: Both chat messages are a timing exchange ('How long will you be?' / 'About 5 min, traffic') [F8][F9], the driver's statement is a bare 'I was on my way' [F11], and the complaint is about the fee [F2]; no threat, abuse, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no escalation under SAFE-1.
